text:
Vince Dunn is playing in a contract year, and NHL Trade Rumors reports the Kraken are making a serious run at an extension. That is worth knowing, because his early numbers tell two stories. He has nine points in 15 games, four on the power play, which is right on his usual pace. And Seattle has been buried at 5v5 with him on the ice: under 38% of the shot attempts and about 43% of the chances, worse than the team does without him.

Some of that is circumstance. Evolving-Hockey had him playing with some of the weakest teammates of any defenseman last season, which makes raw on-ice numbers look worse than his own effect, and his teammates are converting 4.2 goals below their chances when he is out. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows the appeal (he gets to the dangerous ice in front of the net more than almost any defenseman) and the flaw: only 31% of his exits kept possession, so watch for clears and icings under a heavy forecheck. Four points in his last ten against about six and a half expected. A quiet stretch, not a collapse.
headline: Vince Dunn's contract year starts quietly
